ai.description: This small frog measures 18–22 mm. It features a yellowish-green dorsum with dark brown markings and distinct bright yellow irises. A prominent white spot is present on the snout tip.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes flaviocularis* is best distinguished by its distinct, bright yellow iris, which contrasts sharply with the reddish-brown coloration of its iris-less congeners.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes flaviocularis* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically found above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: *Raorchestes flaviocularis* is a nocturnal frog that remains active at night, often found perched on leaves where it hunts for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes flaviocularis* undergoes direct development within terrestrial eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with clutches laid in leaf litter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes flaviocularis* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation evergreen forests above 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes flaviocularis* consists of a series of high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in mid-elevation forests.
